newsitem.title: ITALY: Enel studies French answer to Nigerian gas problem.
newsitem.headline: Enel studies French answer to Nigerian gas problem.

text.p: Italian utility Enel is looking to France to help solve a long-running problem over a liquefied gas contract it has with Nigeria, Enel's managing director Francesco Tato told a conference on Wednesday.
Enel has a contract to buy 3.5 billion cubic metres of Nigerian natural gas a year for the next 25 years, but does not have the capacity in Italy to process it.
Enel suspended the contract last year and Nigeria and Italy held talks aimed at reaching an amicable out-of-court settlement over the cancellation.
But Tato said he was now thinking of sending the liquefied gas to France, which has the processing capacity, and take in return Russian gas imported into France.
"The solution that is being studied would be to give (the gas) to France exchanging it with gas coming from Russia," Tato said. He did not go into further details.
